theory.text: Decide whether a statement agrees with the writer’s opinion or claim. YES: agrees; NO: contradicts the writer’s stance; NOT GIVEN: the writer’s view cannot be established. A viewpoint attributed to another person is not necessarily the writer’s own.
Key skills: Evaluative language, stance and attribution.

guide.text: Find the claim  locate the discussion  distinguish the writer’s opinion from quoted opinions  compare the stance  decide YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

small.text: Text: “In my view, community gardens deserve greater public funding. Some critics argue that they serve too few residents.”
E1. The writer supports increased funding.E2. The writer believes community gardens are a poor investment.E3. The writer thinks gardens should charge visitors.

full.text: Some transport planners argue that wider roads are the best response to congestion. I disagree. Expanding roads may briefly ease delays, but cities should instead improve frequent and reliable public transport. Better bus services can give commuters practical alternatives to driving. I do not suggest that private cars should be banned entirely.
Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.1. The writer prefers public transport improvements to road widening.2. The writer recommends banning all private cars.3. The writer believes train tickets should be free.

rows: The writer supports greater public funding.
The writer advocates for the gardens, not against investment.
The writer says cities should improve public transport instead.
The writer explicitly does not recommend banning all private cars.
No view on free train tickets is provided.
Choosing FALSE when evidence is missing
Use FALSE only if the passage contradicts the statement; otherwise consider NOT GIVEN.

Recheck NO MORE THAN ... WORDS instructions and spelling.
Check the complete sentence against evidence.

Move on and return after easier questions.
Confusing a quoted opinion with the writer’s stance
